title: Introduction to ML Pipelines
body: Machine learning pipelines automate the workflow from raw data to deployed models. This article covers the key components: data ingestion, preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and deployment.

title: Data Engineering with AI
body: Modern data engineering increasingly relies on AI to automate schema inference, data quality checks, and transformation logic. We explore how LLMs can assist data engineers in building robust pipelines.

title: Favnir: Type-Safe AI ETL
body: Favnir is a type-safe pipeline-first language designed for AI data engineering. Its effect system tracks LLM calls, vector DB queries, and external API calls at the type level.

title: Vector Databases Explained
body: Vector databases store high-dimensional embeddings and enable semantic search. This article compares Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, and pgvector for production AI workloads.

title: Semantic Search Architecture
body: Building a semantic search system requires three components: an embedding model, a vector database, and a retrieval layer. We walk through a complete implementation using OpenAI and Pinecone.

title: LLM Extraction Patterns
body: Structured data extraction from unstructured text is a key LLM use case. We cover prompt engineering, schema-guided extraction, and validation strategies for production use.

title: Distributed AI Pipelines
body: Running AI pipelines at scale requires distributed execution. This article covers partitioning strategies, checkpoint-based fault tolerance, and cost optimization for large-scale embedding workloads.

title: Kubernetes for Data Workloads
body: Deploying data pipelines on Kubernetes enables autoscaling and resource isolation. We cover CRD-based pipeline orchestration, GPU resource allocation, and monitoring.

title: Cost Optimization for LLM APIs
body: LLM API costs can be significant at scale. We cover batching strategies, model selection, caching, and cost estimation tools to keep AI pipeline costs under control.

title: OpenTelemetry for AI Pipelines
body: Distributed tracing is essential for debugging AI pipelines. This article covers instrumenting LLM calls, vector DB queries, and pipeline stages with OpenTelemetry.
